concepts.caption: Early Bitcoin users paid a premium just to move their own money. Network upgrades since then have made it far cheaper to self-custody and transact. Exact fee figures to be pulled from verified on-chain data before this goes live.

Average Bitcoin transaction or Lightning fee in 2026
A nameable source for both figures, for example mempool.space historical fee data
concepts.novelty: Uses network fee data instead of a consumer price comparison, and the format itself is unused on the current board.
concepts.purpose: Show how Bitcoin's network has matured by contrasting the cost of moving funds then and now.
concepts.rationale: Fee history is underused territory with a clean two-column format sitting completely empty on the board.
concepts.source_ref: No existing item uses the then_now format, which sits at zero on the board despite being built for exactly this kind of verified historical contrast.
concepts.subject: Bitcoin network fees over time
concepts.target_feeling: Quiet confidence that the technology keeps improving, not a price-driven feeling.
concepts.visual_direction: Two-column layout, left labeled 2017, right labeled 2026. One simple coin icon per side, no numbers on the image itself. A single thin accent-orange divider line down the middle, nothing else in frame. Avoid any chart elements or invented axis values.

concepts.caption: Headlines blame self-custody when a wallet gets hacked. The real issue is almost always bad code, a scam, or a mistake, not the idea of holding your own keys. Done right, self-custody keeps your Bitcoin fully in your control.
flags: self-custody safety framing, confirm wording doesn't imply a security guarantee
concepts.headline: SELF-CUSTODY ISN'T THE PROBLEM. BAD CODE IS.
concepts.mock_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 1080 1350" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="0" y="0" width="1080" height="1350" fill="#FFFFFF"/><text x="540" y="580" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="58" fill="#3D3D3D" text-anchor="middle">SELF-CUSTODY ISN'T</text><text x="540" y="660" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="58" fill="#3D3D3D" text-anchor="middle">THE PROBLEM.</text><text x="540" y="760" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="58" fill="#111111" text-anchor="middle">BAD CODE IS.</text><rect x="980" y="1290" width="60" height="30" fill="#BFBFBF"/></svg>
needs_check: Confirm this reframing doesn't read as a security guarantee claim, a quick compliance sanity check since it is not from the pre-approved copy list.
concepts.novelty: Addresses a security-blame concern directly rather than the freedom-from-seizure angle the existing prop covers, and uses type only instead of an object metaphor.
concepts.purpose: Reframe self-custody security headlines toward the real cause, software quality, not the concept of holding your own keys.
concepts.rationale: Strong-performing security-trust theme from the archive, not yet turned into a visual.
concepts.source_ref: Self-custody isn't the problem here. Bad code is. (157 likes, 2026-07-31), theme: self-custody confidence against hack headlines.
concepts.subject: Self-custody blame reframed to code
concepts.target_feeling: Reassured, and a little sharper about who to actually blame.
concepts.visual_direction: No imagery, type only. Weight 'BAD CODE IS' in Relai orange, the rest in black or dark grey. Generous white space around the line, logo bottom right. Avoid any icon or illustration.

concepts.caption: A new round of real reviews from Relai users, quoted exactly as posted, with country and source link. No edits, no added claims.
concepts.headline: IN THEIR OWN WORDS

needs_check: Source and confirm the exact text of each new review used, with name, country, and public URL, from app store or Trustpilot before building.
concepts.novelty: Same template, entirely new set of reviews not yet used, to keep the feed from repeating the same quotes.
concepts.purpose: Keep social proof fresh with a new set of real user reviews.
concepts.rationale: Testimonial format is underused at just one entry, and social proof keeps the feed credible between bigger concepts.
concepts.source_ref: testimonial format, rerunning 'Review of the week' with a fresh batch of quoted reviews.
concepts.subject: New customer reviews showcase
concepts.target_feeling: Trust built from someone else's words, not the brand's.
concepts.visual_direction: Carousel, one review per slide, consistent card template: quote centered, name and country below in small type, a single Relai orange rule separating quote from attribution. Source URL in tiny type in the corner. No stars, no icons, no photos.

concepts.caption: Buying the same small amount every week adds up in sats, no matter what the price does day to day. This carousel walks through five years of a fixed weekly purchase, one step at a time, using Relai's own backtest data. Figures to be confirmed before publishing.
flags: past performance framing, uses historical price data to compute sats even though no value or return is stated
concepts.headline: WATCH THE SATS ADD UP

needs_check: Exact weekly fiat amount and resulting sats total per year, pulled from Relai's own backtest tool with a confirmed historical BTC price series before any numbers go on the slides.
concepts.novelty: Shows sats accumulated from consistent buying, a positive mechanic, rather than the cost eroded by inflation, and never states a fiat value or return.
concepts.purpose: Demonstrate the DCA mechanic concretely by showing sats accumulate step by step over years.
concepts.rationale: step_compounding sits at zero on the board despite being built for exactly this DCA mechanic.
concepts.source_ref: step_compounding sits at zero on the board despite matching this exact mechanic, and no current item shows sats accumulating slide by slide.
concepts.subject: Weekly DCA sats accumulation over time
concepts.target_feeling: Calm sense that consistency compounds, no excitement, no urgency.
concepts.visual_direction: Carousel, same layout each slide: a single running sat counter in large type, advancing one year per slide, no chart or price line. One accent color on the counter digits. Keep every slide visually identical except the number. Avoid any currency symbols or price mentions on the image.

concepts.caption: You can't own a whole Bitcoin and that's fine. One Bitcoin splits into 100,000,000 sats, so everyone can hold a piece, one sat at a time.
concepts.headline: THERE ARE ENOUGH SATOSHIS.

needs_check: Confirm 100,000,000 sats per Bitcoin, a standard public protocol fact.
concepts.novelty: No existing single_prop covers Bitcoin's divisibility; all current ones use custody or control metaphors instead.
concepts.purpose: Explain Bitcoin divisibility so people who think a whole Bitcoin is out of reach see a path in.
concepts.rationale: single_prop is a cheap, strong format and no existing prop covers divisibility, a real adoption blocker worth addressing.
concepts.source_ref: There's not going to be enough Bitcoin for everyone... but there are enough Satoshis. (archive X post, 104 likes, 2025-05-08)
concepts.subject: Bitcoin divisibility into satoshis
concepts.target_feeling: Relief, this is more accessible than I thought.
concepts.visual_direction: Single object: an orange sliced into many small segments, centered on generous white space. No other props, no text besides the headline. Avoid turning this into a scene with multiple objects.

concepts.caption: Five things people say before they buy their first Bitcoin, and the plain answer to each. No pressure, no hype, just the reasoning laid out.
flags: advice framing risk, confirm answers read as educational not directive
concepts.headline: FIVE EXCUSES, ANSWERED

needs_check: Confirm each one-line answer reads as educational framing, not investment advice, before finalizing the five excuses and responses.
concepts.novelty: Covers procrastination excuses about starting, not technical misconceptions about how Bitcoin works.
concepts.purpose: Pre-empt the common reasons people delay buying their first Bitcoin with calm, plain answers.
concepts.rationale: myth_rebuttal works well twice already; procrastination excuses are a distinct, common objection not yet covered.
concepts.source_ref: myth_rebuttal format, rerunning on a new topic: common excuses for delaying rather than misconceptions about Bitcoin itself.
concepts.subject: Common excuses for not buying Bitcoin
concepts.target_feeling: Gently nudged past hesitation, not pressured.
concepts.visual_direction: Carousel, consistent template each slide: the excuse in quotes at top, the one-line answer directly under it in Relai orange, generous white space around both. No icons, no photos, identical layout every slide.

concepts.caption: Set an amount, pick a frequency, and the auto-invest plan buys Bitcoin for you into self-custody, every time. No need to time the market or remember to tap buy.

concepts.caption: Self-custody means no one else holds your keys. Not an exchange, not an app, not a third party. If you don't hold your own keys, you don't fully control your Bitcoin. Move it into self-custody when you're ready.
concepts.headline: SELF-CUSTODY YOUR BITCOIN. NOT TOMORROW. NOW.
concepts.mock_svg: <svg viewBox="0 0 1080 1350" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect x="0" y="0" width="1080" height="1350" fill="#FFFFFF"/><text x="540" y="520" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="68" fill="#3D3D3D" text-anchor="middle">SELF-CUSTODY YOUR BITCOIN.</text><text x="540" y="640" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="54" fill="#3D3D3D" text-anchor="middle">NOT TOMORROW.</text><text x="540" y="780" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="90" fill="#111111" text-anchor="middle">NOW.</text><rect x="980" y="1290" width="60" height="30" fill="#BFBFBF"/></svg>
concepts.novelty: Only other type_only item is a checklist aimed at businesses; this is a direct consumer-facing imperative about self-custody timing, single statement not a list.
concepts.purpose: Reinforce the self-custody call to action as a standalone, shareable statement for feed and stories.
concepts.rationale: Format is cheap to build and under-used (one item on the board), the line is already compliance-approved so only the visual needs sign-off, and it fills a clean evergreen slot without touching price or savings language.
concepts.source_ref: "Self-custody your Bitcoin. Not tomorrow. Now." from the approved copy pool, line breaks tightened to fit the type treatment
concepts.subject: self-custody urgency, no delay
concepts.target_feeling: A quiet nudge that feels urgent but not pushy, prompting action rather than fear.
concepts.visual_direction: Type only, no imagery. Three stacked lines, each smaller than the last, ending on NOW in the accent orange while the rest stays black on white. Generous margin on all sides. Avoid any icon, lock, or key graphic, the words alone carry it. Logo bottom right.
